result_text:
I fixed the three broken default conventions in `ScopingConventions.java`. The module compiles offline, but I did not confirm the new patterns against sample files: no existing test covers scoping, and my attempt to write a sample-matching script under `/tmp` was refused.

All changes are in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`:

- **Generated HTML (`addGeneratedConventions`):** the pkgdown, Doxygen and `<meta name="generator">` rules now match `(html|htm|xhtml)` instead of `(html|html|xhtml)`. `.html` and `.xhtml` still match, and `.htm` is now covered.
- **Generated .NET docs and JS (`addGeneratedConventions`):** the path patterns changed from `.*/[.]xml` to `.*[.]xml` and from `.*/[.]js` to `.*[.]js`. They now match `MyAssembly.xml` and `app.js`. The content patterns (`<doc>` in the first 2 lines, `// Generated by` in the first line) still gate them, so ordinary `.xml` and `.js` files stay out.
- **Gradle JS (`addBuildAndDeploymentConventions`):** the path pattern changed from `.*[.][-]gradle[.]js` to `.*[-]gradle[.]js`, so `build-gradle.js` matches. `build.gradle` is still matched by the separate `.*[.]gradle` rule.

Path patterns are matched against the whole path, so these changes follow the regex semantics the code already uses. I did not change the content patterns, so `[<]doc[>]` still has to match a whole line, which is how the code already behaves.

Nothing is committed.
